\begin{theorem}\label{night:P3F.7}
\StatementRecord{night:P3F.7}{proved}{}{Definitions and the displayed constructions; \cite[pp.~504--505]{KervaireMilnor1963}; \cite[Theorem 1.2, pp.~404--405, and Corollary 6.6, p.~422]{Haefliger1966}; \cite[Section 2, p.~2091, and Theorem 4.1, pp.~2094--2095]{HarveyKerinShankar2020}}
Retain the AC26 reference sphere and its reference cusp fan, identified explicitly in \cref{iv:source_transports}, with the literal cocharacter \(e_2=\widehat\delta\). Its circle orbit pair is \((S^5,S^2)\); the fixed normal bundle is \(\mathcal O(-1)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)\) with weights \((-1,+1)\). The specified equivariant conifold replacement is free with quotient \(S^2\times S^3\).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\item For the AC26 sphere member, its delta circle is semifree, has one fixed curve F=P1, and its orbit pair is diffeomorphic to the standard pair \(S5,S2\). Its fixed normal bundle is \(\mathcal O(-1)\) plus \(\mathcal O(-1)\) with respective weights\(-1,+1\). Replacing that fixed neighbourhood by the conifold smoothing gives a free circle manifold S3 times S3, with quotient S2 times S3.

\item The original marked $\delta$-circle, its free action off the cusp,
the single fixed rational curve, and its weights are the cited
reference-model calculation
\cite[Proposition~9.24 and Remarks~9.25--9.26, pp.~82--83]{AC26}.
The cocharacter is exactly the source's $e_2=\widehat\delta$ in the
same ordered period lattice. Hence every nonidentity finite subgroup
has that same fixed curve and the action is semifree. We retain the
following actual normal and conifold maps to identify its replacement
and the physical line used by the family.

\item For the vertical wall use the four rays

\[
 r_0=(0,0,1),\quad r_1=(0,1,1),\quad
 r_+=(1,0,1),\quad r_-=(-1,1,1).
\]

\item They satisfy \(r_++r_-=r_0+r_1\). The two adjacent unimodular charts have coordinates \((x_0,x_1,z)\) and \((x'_0,x'_1,z')\), with exact transition

\[
 x'_0=zx_0,\qquad x'_1=zx_1,\qquad z'=1/z,\qquad
 q=x_0x_1z=x'_0x'_1z'.
\]

\item The fixed curve is \(x_0=x_1=0\). The transitions give \(\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2}\), and the cocharacter \(e_2\) has weights \((-1,+1,0)\). The two displayed transition equations give the stated normal degrees and circle weights. Substitution in the following coordinate map checks the conifold equation directly. The map

\[
 A=x_0,\qquad B=zx_0,\qquad C=x_1,\qquad D=zx_1
\]

contracts the curve to \(AD=BC\). It intertwines the circle with weights \(-1,-1,+1,+1\) on \((A,B,C,D)\). On \(AD-BC=\varepsilon\ne0\) the action is free. For \(\varepsilon=1\), polar decomposition of \(SL_2(\mathbb C)\) as \(UH\) gives the explicit equivariant diffeomorphism with \(SU(2)\times\mathbb R^3\), with the circle acting on \(U\) by left multiplication and acting trivially on \(H\). A compact Milnor neighbourhood is thus \(S^3\times D^3\) and its quotient is \(S^2\times D^3\).

\item For completeness, the orbit is identified integrally. Let \(A=X\setminus F\) and \(B=A/S^1\). General position gives \(\pi_1(A)=0\). Alexander duality gives \(H^*(A;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z\) in degrees \(0,3\) and zero otherwise. The oriented normal link \(S^3\) is a primitive generator of \(H_3(A)\). Its quotient is the normal link \(S^2\), and the circle bundle on these links is the Hopf bundle. In the Gysin sequence, \(e\) generates \(H^2(B)\), and integration \(H^3(A)\to H^2(B)\) is multiplication by \(1\): evaluate on this linked \(S^2\) and its Hopf preimage. Every other positive-degree group of \(B\) vanishes. Also \(\pi_1(B)=0\) by the homotopy sequence of the principal circle bundle.

\item Conjugating the negative-weight line converts the fixed normal bundle to a positive-weight complex bundle \(\mathcal O(1)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)\). Its clutching loop \(\operatorname{diag}(z,z^{-1})\) in \(SU(2)\) bounds the explicit disc with \(SU(2)\) coordinates \((a,b)=(\sin(\pi r/2)e^{i\theta},\cos(\pi r/2))\); joining its centre to the identity gives a nullhomotopy. Thus it is a trivial unitary rank-two bundle. Its orbit normal bundle is a trivial oriented rank-three bundle. With this trivialization the boundary is \(F\times S^2\), and the Euler class is just the meridian generator, with no \(F\) term.

\item Now \(Y=X/S^1\) is the union of \(B\) (truncated at that boundary) and \(F\times D^3\). The maps on \(H_0\) and \(H_2\) in Mayer--Vietoris, with domain \(H_2\) ordered as \((F,\text{meridian})\) and target ordered as \((\text{complement},\text{tube})\), are respectively

\[
 \begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]

\item The latter has determinant \(1\). The group \(H_4(\text{boundary})=\mathbb Z\) maps to zero and gives \(H_5(Y)=\mathbb Z\); every other positive intermediate group is zero. The determinant, the conifold coordinate identity and the smooth \(SU(2)\) contraction are checked by \path{code/current_audits/audit_corrections/code/independent_IV_low_F_completion.py}, with exact output in \path{code/current_audits/audit_corrections/code/independent_IV_low_F_completion.json}. Van Kampen gives \(\pi_1(Y)=0\). Thus \(Y\) is a homotopy \(5\)-sphere. Kervaire--Milnor's order table on p.~504 and the Smale comparison on p.~505 give \(\Theta_5=0\), so \(Y\) is diffeomorphic to \(S^5\). Haefliger's Corollary~6.6 gives \(C_n^q=0\) for \(n<2q-3\); with \(n=2,q=3\), and Theorem~1.2 converting concordance to isotopy, every embedding \(S^2\) in \(S^5\) is unknotted. This identifies the orbit pair.

\item One may now construct the equivariant identification with the standard circle action on the sphere boundary of \(D^3\times D^4\). On the free complement the principal circle bundle over \(S^2\times D^3\) has Euler generator and is the product Hopf bundle \(S^3\times D^3\). On the fixed tube it is the trivial positive-weight rank-two bundle just constructed. Their two boundary identifications differ by a gauge map from \(S^2\times S^2\to S^1\). Such a map has a global logarithm because \(H^1(S^2\times S^2;\mathbb Z)=0\), so it extends over a collar and removes the discrepancy. This gives an equivariant diffeomorphism. It is also the specialization of Levine's classification as stated in Harvey--Kerin--Shankar, Theorem~4.1, whose hypotheses are checked here: smooth codimension-four fixed set and \(H^2(F;\mathbb Z)\) without \(2\)-torsion. Replacing the fixed tube \(S^2\times D^4\) by the free piece \(D^3\times S^3\) doubles the free complement, giving \(S^3\times S^3\); the quotient doubles \(S^2\times D^3\), giving \(S^2\times S^3\). The normal framing is unique up to homotopy because \(\pi_2(SO(4))=0\). This is the asserted conifold surgery.

\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}




\begin{theorem}\label{night:P3F.8}
\StatementRecord{night:P3F.8}{proved}{}{\SeriesRef{night:P2.1}, \cref{night:P3F.4}, \cref{night:P3F.7}, \cref{iv:correction:P3K.6}, \cref{night:P3K.7}, \cref{night:P3K.9}}
\par\noindent\textit{Dependency scope.} We use \cref{iv:correction:P3K.6} only at their stated retained-construction or corrected-conclusion scopes.


Retain the parameter loop and sixfold marking of \SeriesRef{night:P2.1}, the complex orientation, and the reference fan and \(e_2\)-circle of \cref{night:P3F.7}. The actual positive equivariant return \(\Phi\), trivialized on the fixed normal tube, descends to a Torelli map \(f\) of \(S^2\times S^3\). The explicit cut-and-reglue map in the proof identifies the oriented sphere clutched by \(\Phi\) with the Hopf gluing \(\lambda(f)\) of \cref{night:P3F.4}.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\item Let \(\Phi\) be the actual positive parameter return map of the sphere family, with the complex orientation, represented by an equivariant Ehresmann trivialization. There is a Torelli diffeomorphism \(f\) of \(S^2\times S^3\), supported in \(S^2\times D^3\), for which the oriented sphere clutched by \(\Phi\) is exactly the Hopf-lift gluing \(\lambda(f)\) of P3F.4. This statement identifies the morphism; it does not assume values of the two integer invariants of \(f\).

\item The parameter family carries the \(\delta\)-circle action. Its fixed curves form a \(\mathbb P^1\)-bundle around the parameter circle; the two normal weight lines have degree \(-1\). The fixed-curve bundle is smoothly trivial because \(PGL_2(\mathbb C)\) is connected. Each weight line over \(\mathbb P^1\times S^1\) is isomorphic as a smooth complex line bundle to the pullback of \(\mathcal O(-1)\), since \(H^2(\mathbb P^1\times S^1;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z\). Thus its equivariant normal disc bundle can be trivialized around the parameter circle. Choose an Ehresmann connection agreeing with that trivialization near the fixed set; averaging over the compact circle makes it equivariant. Its return map is the identity near the fixed tube.

\item Under P3F.7 write the sphere as

\[
 (S^2_y\times D^4_u)\cup(D^3_y\times S^3_u),
\]

with the circle the Hopf action on the \(u\) coordinate. Conjugating the negative normal line reverses its real two-plane orientation; choose the orientation of the \(y\) factor so that this identification preserves the complex orientation of \(X\). The restriction of \(\Phi\) to the free part is an equivariant map \(\widetilde f\) of \(D^3_y\times S^3_u\) equal to the identity near its boundary. Its quotient is a map of \(D^3_y\times S^2_u\) relative boundary. Extend it by the identity over the other hemisphere of \(S^3_y\). This defines \(f:S^3_y\times S^2_u\to S^3_y\times S^2_u\). It fixes the \(H_2\) generator, since that generator is represented in the identity hemisphere. It preserves orientation, so Poincare duality makes it fix \(H_3\) as well. Consequently \(f\) is in the Torelli group.

\item Its Hopf lift \(A\) on \(S^3_y\times S^3_u\) equals \(\widetilde f\) on the first hemisphere and the identity on the second. Any other lift differs by a gauge map \(S^2\times S^3\to S^1\). Its \(H^1\) is zero, so that map has a global logarithm and yields an isotopy of lifts.

\item Here is the cut-and-reglue comparison. In the standard sphere \(\partial(D^4_u\times D^4_y)\), put

\[
 H=D^4_u\times S^3_y,\qquad K=S^3_u\times D^4_y,\qquad
 N=S^3_u\times D^3_y\subset\partial H=\partial K.
\]

\item Our gluing convention identifies \(x\in\partial H\) with \(A(x)\in\partial K\), after the standard product-boundary identification. The ball \(B^7=D^4_u\times D^3_y\) has boundary \(N\cup(D^4_u\times S^2_y)\). Its complement in the rounded product boundary is the other standard \(7\)-ball: this follows by taking the two hemispheres of the \(y\) boundary and rounding their product collars. Regluing \(H\) to \(K\) by \(A\) changes the identification only on \(N\). Equivalently cut out \(B^7\) and reglue its boundary by the map equal to \(\widetilde f\) on \(N\) and the identity on \(D^4_u\times S^2_y\). That boundary map is precisely \(\Phi\) in the displayed decomposition of \(S^6\). The identity on the common collar makes the two quotient constructions coincide pointwise outside \(N\), and their collar identifications coincide on \(N\). Hence

\[
 D^7\cup_\Phi D^7=(D^4_u\times S^3_y)\cup_A(S^3_u\times D^4_y)
\]

as oriented smooth manifolds, with outward boundary orientation on the first piece and the complex sphere orientation used to choose the initial identification. This is \(\lambda(f)\).

\item The actual sixfold descent of P2.1 is

\[
 H(t)\delta,\qquad
 H(t)=-\frac{4\ell_1\log t+3\ell_2\log(t-1)}{2\pi i},
\]

with cusp coefficient \(-p\) after carrying the collar integer \(\ell_0\). P3K.6--7 constructs its real trace with the complete line clutch. \cref{night:P3K.9} evaluates the meridian-line pair as
\((-6,-24)\), with descended pair \((-1,-4)\). The explicit
extending duality \(U=M^{-1}\) gives the physical pairs
\((6,24)\) and \((1,4)\), respectively, with that same
normal-frame comparison. The forward geometric mapping-torus orientation and Jin's reverse convention are both included in P3K.7.

\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}




\begin{theorem}\label{night:P3F.9}
\StatementRecord{night:P3F.9}{proved}{}{Definitions and the displayed constructions}
For the reference cusp model and specified small resolution used in \cref{night:P3F.7}, retain the opposite physical-circle weights, the marked \(\gamma\)-circle and the prescribed outer stable framing. The resolved cusp orbit has a relative product comparison with a nodal elliptic neighbourhood times that marked circle, and the derivative of the comparison preserves the given stable outer framing up to the displayed relative homotopy.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\item The local calculation giving the product is as follows. Start with the ordinary conifold \(xy=uv\), with the circle acting on \(u,v\) with weights \(+1,-1\) and fixing \(x,y\). A small resolution has charts

\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (x,v,z):&\quad u=xz,\quad y=vz;\\
 (u,y,w):&\quad x=uw,\quad v=yw,\quad w=1/z.
 \end{aligned}
\]

\item The orbit charts, with the Hopf smoothing defined using these normal coordinates, are

\[
 (x,y,b),\quad b=\frac{|z|^2-|v|^2}{2};\qquad
 (x,y,b'),\quad b'=\frac{|u|^2-|w|^2}{2}.
\]

\item On the overlap \(r=|z|^2>0\) they satisfy

\[
 2b=r-\frac{|y|^2}{r},\qquad
 2b'=|x|^2r-\frac1r,\qquad
 \frac{db'}{db}=\frac{|x|^2+r^{-2}}{1+|y|^2r^{-2}}>0.
 \tag{P3F.9.1}
\]

\item Thus projection to\(x,y\) is a smooth submersion with oriented one-dimensional fibres. Every fibre is a line: away from\(x,y\)=\(0,0\) the two charts join its negative and positive ends in the displayed increasing order; over\(0,0\) the exceptional interval joins the two half-lines. A smooth section can be chosen in the free part. For \(\varepsilon>0\) choose the unique \(r>0\) solving

\[
 |x|^2r-\frac{|y|^2}{r}+2\varepsilon\frac{r-1}{r+1}=0.
\]

\item The left side increases strictly from a negative to a positive value; its derivative is \(|x|^2+|y|^2/r^2+4\varepsilon/(r+1)^2>0\). Consequently \(r\) is a smooth positive function of \((x,y)\), and the representatives \(z=\sqrt r\), \(v=y/\sqrt r\), \(u=x\sqrt r\) give the section in the orbit. A positive vertical vector field, patched by a partition of unity and rescaled to be complete, identifies each line with \(\mathbb R\) by flow from this section. It therefore gives a product diffeomorphism over \(\mathbb C^2\).

\item This comparison can be made relative to a prescribed product identification outside the node neighbourhood. The quotient smoothing uses a choice of invariant metric in the fixed normal bundle; choose it to agree with the original product normal metric outside that neighbourhood. There projection to\(x,y\) is the original smooth submersion. On overlapping local line trivialisations the transitions are increasing by\(P3F.9.1\). Taking a partition of unity on the base and a convex combination of increasing, proper fibre coordinates produces an increasing proper coordinate agreeing with the prescribed one where the outer partition has weight one. This is a relative product trivialization. Its derivative over the fixed \(x,y\) base is an upper triangular real matrix with identity base block and a positive fibre derivative. Contracting the off-diagonal block and then the positive scalar gives a homotopy to the identity relative to the prescribed outer product. Thus this comparison retains the stable boundary framing, not just the orbit diffeomorphism type. In particular one must not equate all quadratic invariants in different normal metrics at a fixed point: their transition can involve a radial square root. The metric choice and the positive-coordinate construction avoid that error.

\item Apply this calculation to the square Mumford fan before triangulation. The square model is the fibre product of the two nodal elliptic models; the \(A_2\) triangulation is its small resolution, one per lattice cell. The circle acts in the second nodal factor. Its orbit is a smooth circle bundle over the base disc, since its local quotient at the node is\((q,b)=(uv,(|u|^2-|v|^2)/2)\). It is a product over the disc. Before resolving the conifold, the total orbit is therefore \(E_{I_1}\times S^1\), where \(E_{I_1}\) is a compact neighbourhood of one nodal elliptic fibre in a smooth elliptic surface. The relative comparison above replaces the node orbit without changing this product diffeomorphism type or its outer boundary marking.

\item The bounded toric units of the actual construction do not change this statement. Choose their logarithms on the cusp disc. Their interpolation to constant units gives the same unimodular charts and a proper smooth family after shrinking the disc uniformly; the logarithmic terms dominate every bounded unit. Averaging an Ehresmann field gives an equivariant comparison. In the source elliptic factor, the \(\gamma\) deck translates by the section \(6P\). Its Tate coordinate is a unit \(a(q)\), and the explicit path \(Z\mapsto\exp(t\log a(q))Z\) extends across the nodal fibre. Its suspension is consequently a product \(E_{I_1}\times S^1_\gamma\). The source Picard line restricted to an elliptic neighbourhood selected disjoint from the fixed sphere is topologically trivial: its degree on the nodal fibre is zero, and that neighbourhood retracts onto the nodal fibre. An extending Hermitian metric removes its radial unit on this slice. This statement does not trivialize the principal-circle line on the complement of the fixed sphere in the entire orbit neighbourhood.
